chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalaf from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

While al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was in the lap of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he raised his head and said, 'O my father, what is the reward for one who visits you after your death?' He replied, 'O my son, whoever comes to me as a visitor after my death will have Paradise, and whoever comes to your father as a visitor after his death will have Paradise, and whoever comes to your brother as a visitor after his death will have Paradise, and whoever comes to you as a visitor after your death will have Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Imams after their death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the theological basis for Ziyarat al-Ahl al-Bayt by linking posthumous visitation directly to Paradise. It underscores the unique spiritual status of the Prophet, Imam Ali, Imam Hasan, and Imam Husayn, reflecting the Shia belief that their physical presence serves as a conduit for divine grace even after death.
